title: DR1 lets a rail or road consignment be saved with no transit countries at all; the frontend refuses the page until at least one country is chosen.

finding.frontend: The transited-countries obligation is gated on the means of transport being rail or road, and where it applies its status is mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:93-104). Submitting the page with nothing ticked is rejected with "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.controller.js:38-40). A consignment that crosses no third country — a lorry from the Republic of Ireland, say — has no honest answer to give, and the hub cannot be completed without one.
finding.prototype: DR1 puts the page in the journey under the same condition, when the means of transport is Railway or Road Vehicle, and then lets it be left empty: the handler for the page saves whatever was submitted and redirects onward without validating anything, so pressing Save and continue with no country added takes the user to the next page (app/routes.js:10503-10537). Submission is not blocked either — the review card for transit countries is built with its error state permanently off, under the line "Transit countries are optional for submission" (:4795-4805). DR1 does not call an empty answer finished, though: its hub row for Transit countries reads "To do" until at least one country has been added (:5798-5802). The captured empty state shows Save and continue live with no country in the list.
finding.difference: Drop the at-least-one rule so the page can be saved and left with nothing chosen, and let a rail or road notification reach submission with no transit countries recorded. The gate itself — rail or road only — already matches DR1 and does not change, and neither does the hub: both sides leave the row outstanding while the list is empty, so it is the page and the submission that differ, not the task list. This should land with the change to the control, since both alter the same field. Neither side's captured screen shows the state after pressing Save and continue with nothing chosen, so the claim rests on reading the frontend's validator and DR1's route handler; photographing both sides at that moment would put it beyond argument.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting fe-transit-countries with no country ticked and being taken onward — the controller returns 400 with the "Select at least one country" error whenever the selection is empty, on either button, because it validates before it branches on the exit action.
finding.verification: Read the frontend controller and obligations file whole, read every transit-country function, route and hub row in DR1's app/routes.js, and read the fe-transit-countries screenshot. Ran the falsifier by tracing the frontend's POST: transitedCountriesErrors runs before the exit branch and both buttons post to the same handler, so neither Save and continue nor Save and return to hub can park the page empty; it does not fire. The frontend's gate and mandatory status are as claimed. Rubric 3 fired on the prototype side: the finding's core claim survives but the evidence it rested on is dead code and one consequence it drew is the opposite of what DR1 does. Slots for finding.prototype and finding.difference rewritten; see correction. Band left at frontend-work and confidence left at medium, which is honest — the difference is read out of both sides' handlers and neither side's empty-submit outcome is photographed, and finding.difference names that shot as what would settle it.
finding.correction: Claimed: "DR1 treats the answer as optional: any saved list, empty included, counts as complete", cited to app/routes.js:1932-1935, and from that, work of "make the hub treat an empty list as a complete answer rather than an outstanding one". True: the function at :1932-1935 is hasTransitCountriesComplete, which returns true unconditionally and is never called — grep for its name across app/routes.js returns exactly one hit, its own definition. The live check is hasTransitCountriesSelected, and DR1's hub uses it at :5801 to show the Transit countries row as "To do" until at least one country is added. So DR1's hub does not treat an empty list as complete, and the instruction to make the frontend's hub do so would have driven the frontend away from DR1 rather than toward it. Checked by grepping both helper names, reading the hub section at :5790-5808 and reading the review card at :4795-4805. What survives, and is now what the finding says: DR1's page itself has no validation at all and its review card is built with the error state off under the comment "Transit countries are optional for submission", so a rail or road notification can be carried past the page and submitted with none, while the frontend refuses to leave the page. The hub behaves the same on both sides.

relatedTo.why: the other rule the frontend puts on this field and DR1 does not
